title: Measurement invariance in CB-SEM
summary: Before comparing factor means or paths across groups, test that the measurement model is equivalent, from configural to metric to scalar invariance.

body.text: Group comparisons assume that the instrument measures the same constructs in the same way in every group. [[measurement-invariance]] is tested with a sequence of increasingly constrained multigroup CFAs (Vandenberg & Lance 2000):

items: **Configural:** the same pattern of loadings in every group.
**Metric (weak):** equal loadings; needed to compare relationships such as paths or factor covariances.
**Scalar (strong):** equal intercepts as well; needed to compare factor means.
**Partial invariance:** some parameters freed when full invariance fails, with a substantive justification.

body.text: Each step is compared with the previous one, with a χ² difference test and changes in fit indices; a drop in CFI of no more than .01 is a widely used heuristic (Cheung & Rensvold 2002).
SEM Studio does not run multigroup CFA or invariance tests yet. Export the lavaan script and add the grouping variable (lavaan's `group` and `group.equal` arguments) to test invariance in R.
body.title: Not available in SEM Studio

mistake.title: Comparing latent means without scalar invariance
mistake.text: If intercepts differ between groups, a mean difference may reflect item functioning rather than a difference in the construct.

checks.question: You want to compare the latent mean of satisfaction between two countries. Which level of invariance do you need at least?

options.feedback: Correct. Mean comparisons require equal intercepts.
Configural invariance only shows the same factor pattern; scales may still differ.
Metric invariance supports comparing relationships, not means.

checks.question: Moving from configural to metric invariance, CFI drops from .962 to .958. What does the Cheung and Rensvold heuristic suggest?

options.text: The drop (.004) is within .01, so metric invariance is not rejected on that criterion.
options.feedback: Correct, as a heuristic, alongside the χ² difference test.

options.text: Metric invariance fails because CFI fell.
options.feedback: Constraints always reduce fit somewhat; the question is whether the drop is negligible.

options.text: CFI cannot be used for nested comparisons.
options.feedback: ΔCFI is widely used for exactly this purpose.

checks.explanation: Judge the change, not the direction.
